output_definition: Per scope: predicted log1p(|z|) of the two-session market response (z = abnormal return / trailing sigma), rank-calibrated to a 1-10 EventShock score with an empirical uncertainty interval. Inputs: market state, timing, the frozen text-model outputs (read from the TF-IDF event model impact was fitted with) and the structured calendar (earnings dates, recent 8-K filings, FOMC), each tagged known-before or published-at-event-time.

checks.detail: Spearman of prediction vs realised |z|; pass if the 95% interval's lower bound > 0.0
checks.label: Rank skill on held-out episodes (val+test)

checks.detail: paired difference in log-severity MAE; pass if the 95% interval's upper bound < 0
checks.label: Error vs the constant baseline (val+test)

checks.detail: point difference in log-severity MAE <= 0.002 on each of val and test (R2-ridge)
checks.label: Not worse than the market-state linear model

checks.detail: Spearman of bucket order vs bucket median |z| >= 0.8 (needs >= 4 buckets of >= 10 episodes)
checks.label: Score buckets ordered by realised severity (val+test)

checks.detail: covered share within 0.1 of nominal
checks.label: Realised-score interval coverage (val+test)

checks.detail: feature registry, group straddle, time order + embargo, rolling folds, fit invariance
checks.label: Leakage suite clean

checks.detail: skill that also predicts the window before the event is market state, not the event
checks.label: More skill on the real window than on the pre-event placebo (val+test)

checks.detail: the served documents are news with first-seen or publisher clocks, unlike the 2022 tweets
checks.label: Rank skill on 2026 news with publisher timestamps

checks.detail: from the episode-level evidence study (docs/evidence/impact_study.json; its selected model R3s-full, this artifact's R3s-additive): Spearman after removing the issuer x volatility-bucket regime from prediction and outcome; pass if the lower bound > 0
checks.label: Regime-neutral rank skill (test)

checks.detail: from the episode-level evidence study (docs/evidence/impact_study.json; its selected model R3s-full, this artifact's R3s-additive): paired log-severity MAE difference; pass if the upper bound is below 0 on test and on live
checks.label: Block increment over market state (R3s-full vs R2-full)

checks.detail: from the episode-level evidence study (docs/evidence/impact_study.json; its selected model R3s-full, this artifact's R3s-additive): share of years (>= 100 episodes) where the block's point difference is below zero; pass if >= 0.75
checks.label: The block helps in most calendar years

acceptance.rule: Pre-registered in configs/impact_model.yaml before the first held-out run. PRODUCTION needs every check to pass: C1 rank skill above zero (val+test, 95% interval); C2 lower log-severity error than the constant (paired interval below zero); C3 not worse than the market-state-only linear model on val and on test; C4 predicted-score buckets ordered by realised severity; C5 the served realised-score interval covers close to its nominal share; C6 the leakage suite is clean; C7 more skill on the real window than on the pre-event placebo window; C8 skill on news (2026, publisher timestamps). A check that cannot be evaluated is not a pass.

scopes.algorithm: additive gradient boosting (one feature per interaction group) on log1p(|z|); params {'l2_regularization': 10.0, 'learning_rate': 0.05, 'max_depth': 2, 'max_iter': 250, 'min_samples_leaf': 60}

calibration.method: rank-calibrated: prediction -> percentile of the out-of-fold training predictions -> |z| at the same percentile of the realised severity distribution -> the target's own fixed cut points; interval = what comparable out-of-fold events realised

direction.note: sign of (P(pos) - P(neg)) vs sign of the realised abnormal return; 0.5 is a coin flip. Reported, not used by the score.

evaluations.title: 2026 news, publisher timestamps outside trading hours

ladder.verdict: baseline: the training mean
adopted: beats R0-constant out of fold, interval entirely below zero
not adopted: no significant out-of-fold gain over R2-ridge
not adopted: no significant out-of-fold gain over R2-ridge
adopted: beats R2-ridge out of fold, interval entirely below zero
adopted: beats R2s-ridge out of fold, interval entirely below zero
not adopted: no significant out-of-fold gain over R2s-additive
not adopted: no significant out-of-fold gain over R2s-additive
adopted: beats R2s-additive out of fold, interval entirely below zero
not adopted: no significant out-of-fold gain over R3s-additive

leakage_findings: [INFO] feature_availability: all features are registered event-time features
[INFO] group_straddle: no episode spans two splits (25238 groups)
[INFO] time_order: splits are time ordered with the embargo respected: train 2015-01-02..2023-12-21, val 2024-01-02..2024-12-23, test 2025-01-02..2025-12-31, live 2026-02-17..2026-09-30
[INFO] rolling_folds: 14 rolling-origin folds: every fold trains >= 5 sessions before its test period; no episode straddles
[INFO] fit_invariance: refit with val/test/live labels scrambled gives bit-identical predictions
limitations: Held-out evidence is two calendar years of GDELT news titles (2024 val, 2025 test) plus 2026 news, a deterministic six-slots-a-day sample of GDELT (about 6% of the flow), titles only. Far larger than impact-v1's 2022 hold-out, but still one regime; it says nothing about a crisis year it never saw.

Most of what the model predicts is the volatility regime: it predicts the window BEFORE the event better than the window after it (check C7). The event-specific part is the structured calendar (mainly: an earnings release is expected, or an earnings 8-K was just filed), worth about two percent of the error; the text-model outputs add nothing measurable once the calendar is known.
The target is a coincident market-response proxy: coverage is partly a reaction to a move, so this is not a clean forecast.
34 current large caps: severity is calibrated for them and does not transfer to small or distressed issuers (survivorship).

The calendar is read from SEC EDGAR acceptance times and the Federal Reserve's published meeting dates: scheduled-meeting dates are announced ahead, but they were read from a 2026 snapshot. An earnings date is inferred from the issuer's own earlier filings, not from an announced date.
Consensus earnings estimates are not free data, so the realised earnings surprise is never an input; only whether and when earnings are expected.
Checks C9-C11 are computed at the episode level by the evidence study; the other checks are computed here at the level the model serves. A scope that fails any check is experimental.
